issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies an Animal constructor with two parameters (Animal(String, int)), but the provided template/solution use and implement a single-parameter constructor (Animal(String)). This mismatch will confuse students about which constructor to implement and may cause tests or provided example code to fail if they follow the UML instead of the template/solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML to require Animal(String) (and remove the age parameter), or (B) update the template and solution to add the age attribute and a two-argument constructor Animal(String, int), adjusting all subclass constructors and example usages accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares an age attribute (age: int) for Animal, while the solution (and example usage in the template) do not declare or initialize any age field. The textual description elsewhere only mentions that animals have a name, creating an internal inconsistency in the problem specification and a mismatch with the solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the inconsistency by aligning the problem text/UML with the implementation. Either (A) remove the age attribute from the UML and from any textual references so the spec clearly requires only a name field, or (B) add an int age field to the Animal implementation (with constructor, getter/setter) and update examples and subclass constructors accordingly.
